subject: Purchase order field gaps for Coupa enrollment — vendor onboarding & MSA alignment
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@northbridgehealth.com>, NorthBridge Health Procurement <procurement@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Purchase order field gaps for Coupa enrollment — vendor onboarding & MSA alignment

Hi Liam / NB Procurement team,

Quick note from onboarding: your Coupa registration is failing the final validation step because several PO fields we expect are missing or labeled differently in your sample POs. I attached a short PO_Field_Mapping.xlsx that maps what Coupa is sending today vs. what our order ingestion expects. The main gaps are: buyer_code (sometimes "buyerID"), cost_center (optional in your sample), and commodity_code (missing). Also currency codes are sometimes lowercase which breaks our downstream parsers.

Two asks:
- Can you share a sample PO from a live order (we saw Sample_PO_000123 but need one with cost_center filled)?
- Legal: we need a quick alignment on a small MSA clause to make clear that receipt of a valid PO constitutes acceptance for delivery/payment terms (this avoids ambiguity when field names vary). I tagged Kimberly on this email.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to propose a 1-paragraph MSA addendum (legal) — target EOD tomorrow.
2) Dev to confirm which field name aliases we can support as a short-term fix.
3) Once legal approves, Marissa to publish an Order Form template that calls out required fields for Coupa onboarding.

I've included a Drive link with the mapping and a DocuSign placeholder for the redline if needed.

Attachments: PO_Field_Mapping.xlsx

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales (Vendor Onboarding)
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0167

Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Purchase order field gaps for Coupa enrollment — vendor onboarding & MSA alignment

Hi Hannah — thanks for the heads up and the mapping doc. I attached a cleaner sample PO (Sample_PO_000123.pdf) that includes cost_center and buyerID fields; however our supplier team sometimes omits commodity_code on low-dollar orders.

On tax: we typically collect and forward tax jurisdiction but we do not reconcile tax amounts on our side — we expect vendors to invoice net and indicate tax separately. If you need us to populate a specific tax_jurisdiction field, let me know the exact key name.

We can ask our Coupa admin to enable a "commodity_code" field as mandatory for Redwood on our side if that will unblock you.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Procurement Manager, NorthBridge Health
liam.oconnor@northbridgehealth.com | (617) 555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Purchase order field gaps for Coupa enrollment — vendor onboarding & MSA alignment

Thanks for looping me in. I reviewed the sample PO and the mapping. Two short legal edits I recommend to avoid future ambiguity:

1) Acceptance by PO: Add an MSA addendum clause — "Notwithstanding any contrary language, the parties agree that Redwood's receipt of a purchase order that references this Agreement and contains the required PO fields (buyer_code, cost_center, commodity_code) shall constitute acceptance of the purchase order and an obligation to perform under the terms of the referenced Order Form."

2) Invoicing/tax: Clarify invoice remittance and tax responsibility — "Vendor shall invoice Redwood per the payment terms in the Order Form. Taxes shall be indicated separately on the invoice; Redwood will not assume responsibility for reconciling third-party tax calculations unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing."

I've prepared a redline (Redline_MSA_v3.pdf) that inserts the above language under Section 2 (Orders & Acceptance) and adds a short note in the Order Form appendix enumerating required PO fields and their aliases.

Operational ask for Dev/Marissa: I recommend adding a short table in the order form that enumerates accepted aliases (e.g., buyer_code, buyerID) and enforcement behavior (required vs optional). That avoids having to re-redline the MSA for each vendor.

I can convert the redline into a DocuSign envelope if everyone is comfortable with the language.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Purchase order field gaps for Coupa enrollment — vendor onboarding & MSA alignment

Thanks — quick technical plan from my side:

- We can accept aliases for buyer_code (buyerID, purchaser_id) and normalize to "buyer_code" in ingestion.
- For cost_center: make field required for Redwood-enabled customers; if missing, set order to "pending:field" status and notify vendor via automated email.
- commodity_code: we can make this optional for low-dollar value orders (< $500) but require it for PO amount >= $500.
- currency case-sensitivity: normalize currency codes to uppercase in parser.

ETA: I can push a Coupa mapping change and test harness by Friday 2026-02-13 EOD. After that, Hannah / Marissa can run a staged end-to-end test with NorthBridge.

Marissa: please confirm who will create the Order Form appendix table (fields + aliases + required rules) and whether you want the MSA redline routed via DocuSign once Kim confirms.

I'll also prepare a short test PO template for Liam so we can run one successful inbound flow and verify invoices parse correctly.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Platform Integrations Engineer, Redwood Inference
